correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact two-agent reduction with self-degree 1+w, verified the first integral by direct differentiation, and classified all trajectories using monotonicity and the unique maximum of Psi at log(2)/alpha. The critical Taylor expansion Psi(dc)-Psi(dc+z)=(alpha/dc)z²+O(z³) gives w~alpha z²/(2dc) and z~2/(alpha t), hence the stated exact inverse-square-time weight coefficient. The global alpha threshold uses d0<=2 and is attained sharply at d0=2. A standalone standard-library checker executed 128 differential-identity/numerical assertions; finite integration is not substituted for proof. Excluded d0=0 and endpoint tie strengths are clearly treated as boundary cases.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial evolving social network supplies a sharp, explicit analytical decision boundary between complete consensus and permanent residual disagreement although interaction phi never vanishes. The nontrivial critical orbit has quantified universal inverse-time and inverse-square-time slowing; the sharp alpha cutoff separates parameters permitting/disallowing such persistent two-agent separation over the entire physically allowed opinion interval. These facts give a structurally motivated validation benchmark for adaptive-opinion simulations and isolate the effect of decaying endogenous ties, rather than constituting an arbitrary special-value calculation.
